title: Canonical direct-image limit comparison as a morphism of Roos triangles
statement:
Let $f:(\mathscr X,R_X)\to(\mathscr Y,R_Y)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with a specified ring isomorphism $f^{-1}R_Y\cong R_X$. Module pullback $F=f^*$ is exact and left adjoint to module direct image $G=f_*$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the ringed-topos convention [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], and strict inverse sequences indexed by $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$.
Assume countable products of module sheaves on both sites are exact. Use $\mathcal G=Rf_*$, $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}=Rf_*^{\rm Tow}$ and the normalized comparison $a_M:\mathcal G R\lim_X M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim_Y\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$ of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison]. For a derived strict tower $M$, the product comparison
$$\alpha_M:\mathcal G\bigl(\prod_n^D M_n\bigr)\longrightarrow\prod_n^D(\mathcal GM_n)$$
with components $\mathcal G(p_n)$ is invertible and commutes with transition endomorphisms, hence with $1-s$. The triple $(a_M,\alpha_M,\alpha_M)$ is a morphism from $\mathcal G$ of the canonical Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit] of $M$ to the canonical Roos triangle of $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$, including the connecting square with the canonical shift comparison. Here $R\lim$ is total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], and the canonical Roos triangle of a derived strict tower $N$ is fixed as follows. For a complex $X$ of strict towers representing $N$, let $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ be the strict Roos model of [def-weil-strict-roos-model], with coordinates $(y,x)\in\prod_nX_n^{r-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^r$. Take its rotated cone triangle $H(X)\xrightarrow{r}\prod_nX_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nX_n\xrightarrow{b}H(X)[1]$, where $r(y,x)=x$ and $b(z)=(z,0)$, with termwise products representing $\prod^D$. Transport it to $R\lim N$ along the isomorphism $Q(H(X))\cong R\lim N$. That isomorphism is the unit-normalized comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-products-roos-comparison], composed with the chain isomorphism $(y,x)\mapsto(-y,x)$ from the fibre of $-(1-s)$ to $H(X)$. On a K-injective $X$ this is transport along the ordinary-limit inclusion with coordinates $(0,(\lambda_n)_n)$. The canonical shift comparison $\sigma$ of $\mathcal G$ is the one compatible with the derived-functor units of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]: $\sigma_{QK}\circ\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]$ for every complex $K$. The first component is precisely the underived-composite normalized $a_M$, rather than an unspecified cone isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(R_Y)$. Their strict tower categories are Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], with small index $\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] in $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$ to choose a representative $q:X\to I$ of $M$, where $I$ is K-injective and every tower $I^r$ is injective. Write $I_n=\operatorname{ev}_n I$, $J=G^{\rm Tow}I$, $P_I=\prod_n I_n$ termwise, $P_J=\prod_n GI_n$, and $L_I=\lim_n I_n$, $L_J=\lim_n GI_n$ termwise. The evaluations $I_n$ are K-injective by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective].

proof.text: The adjunction $F\dashv G$ extends levelwise to $F^{\rm Tow}\dashv G^{\rm Tow}$: the componentwise adjunct of a natural transformation is natural by naturality of the adjunction bijection. Since exactness of towers is levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], $F^{\rm Tow}$ is exact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $J$ K-injective and makes each $GI_n$ K-injective. The same lemma applied to the exact constant-tower functor $\Delta$ left adjoint to $\lim$ makes $L_I$ and $L_J$ K-injective. Moreover $G^{\rm Tow}$ preserves the injective degree terms: a map $U\to G^{\rm Tow}I^r$ across a monomorphism $U\hookrightarrow V$ is adjoint to $F^{\rm Tow}U\to I^r$, which extends across the monomorphism $F^{\rm Tow}U\hookrightarrow F^{\rm Tow}V$ by injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Hence $J$ has injective degree terms too. The K-injective total-derived-functor computation [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] now represents $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$ by $J$, $R\lim_X M$ by $L_I$, and $R\lim_Y(\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M)$ by $L_J$.

proof.text: There are canonical chain isomorphisms $c:G(P_I)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_J$ and $\beta:G(L_I)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_J$. For example, for any $B\in\mathcal B$, the adjunction and the product universal property [def-weil-category-product] identify $\operatorname{Hom}(B,G(\prod I_n^r))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(FB,\prod I_n^r)=\prod\operatorname{Hom}(FB,I_n^r)=\prod\operatorname{Hom}(B,GI_n^r)$; thus $G(\prod I_n^r)$, with legs $G(\pi_n)$, is a product. With compatible families in place of all families, the same bijections show $G(\lim I_n^r)$ is a limit of $GI_n^r$. Uniqueness of maps with these legs makes the degreewise comparisons commute with differentials, and supplies their inverses. In particular $\pi_n c=G(\pi_n)$ and $\lambda_n\beta=G(\lambda_n)$, with $\lambda_n$ the limit legs.

proof.text:
By [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective], $P_I$ and $P_J$ are K-injective and represent the respective products in the derived categories. Also $G(P_I)$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. The identity-resolution identifications of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] therefore identify $Q(c)$ with the statement's $\alpha_M$: its $n$th component is exactly $\mathcal G(p_n)$. Let $u_I=1-s_I$ and $u_J=1-s_J$. Projection to the $n$th factor gives
$\pi_n cG(u_I)=G(\pi_n)-G(t_n)G(\pi_{n+1})=\pi_n u_Jc$,
where $t_n:I_{n+1}\to I_n$. Product uniqueness proves $cG(u_I)=u_Jc$, and hence the claimed transition-endomorphism square as well.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), first proof via the tower-topos square; Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective tower computation. Explicit cone-normalization refinement.

proof.text: Use the explicit model [def-weil-strict-roos-model]: $H_I=\operatorname{Cone}(u_I)[-1]$, with $H_I^r=P_I^{r-1}\oplus P_I^r$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-u_Ix,dx)$, and similarly $H_J$. These are K-injective. Indeed the cone triangle and its rotations in the homotopy category, with [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], imply $\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(A,H_I[k])=0$ for every acyclic $A$ and integer $k$: the adjacent terms are Hom groups into shifts of $P_I$ and are zero by K-injectivity. This proves the defining null-homotopy condition; it also proves the assertion for $H_J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-products-roos-comparison] in each module category: their tower categories are Grothendieck by Step 1 and countable products are exact by hypothesis. This gives the unit-normalized cone comparison with total derived limit. Its convention uses $-u$; the chain isomorphism $(y,x)\mapsto(-y,x)$ to our $u$-cone preserves the zero-first-coordinate inclusion. On the K-injective towers $I,J$, the derived units are invertible, so the inclusions $j_I:L_I\to H_I$, $z\mapsto(0,(\lambda_nz)_n)$, and $j_J:L_J\to H_J$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Hence, by the statement's convention, the canonical Roos triangles of $M$ and of $\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M$ are the rotated cone triangles of $u_I$ and $u_J$, transported along $Q(j_I)$ and $Q(j_J)$. Indeed, the normalized comparison composed with the sign isomorphism sends $Q(j_I)$ to the unit $\eta_I$. That unit is the identification of $R\lim_XM$ with $Q(L_I)$ from Step 2, and likewise for $J$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-roos-additive-comparison] with the additive functor $G$; its product-comparison hypothesis holds for every tower complex by the adjunction calculation in Step 3. It gives the natural chain isomorphism $\theta:G(H_I)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_J$, whose two coordinates are $c^{r-1}$ and $c^r$ after the canonical biproduct comparison. Directly,
$\theta d(y,x)=(-c\,dy-c\,u_Ix,c\,dx)=(-d\,cy-u_Jcx,d\,cx)=d\theta(y,x)$.
Its inverse uses $c^{-1}$ on both coordinates. In particular, the limit-leg equalities of Step 3 give the equality of actual chain maps
$\theta\,G(j_I)=j_J\beta$:
both have zero first coordinate and second coordinate with $n$th leg $G(\lambda_n)$. This verifies the augmentation normalization as well as the cone comparison.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), first proof via the tower-topos square; Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective tower computation. Explicit cone-normalization refinement.

proof.text: The rotated cone triangle has first map $r_I:H_I\to P_I$, $(y,x)\mapsto x$, second map $u_I$, and last map $b_I:P_I\to H_I[1]$, $z\mapsto(z,0)$, with the cone/rotation signs of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-triangulated-category]; likewise for $J$. The diagonal coordinates in Step 6 give $cG(r_I)=r_J\theta$ and $\theta[1]G(b_I)=b_Jc$ after the termwise shift identification; the second equality has coordinates $(cz,0)=(cz,0)$. Since $L_I,P_I,H_I$ are K-injective, their identity-resolution comparisons compute the derived functor, including these maps [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. The shift $[1]$ is an automorphism of complexes that commutes with $Q$ and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. So $(\mathcal G\circ[1],\eta_{-[1]})$ is a total derived functor of $G\circ[1]=[1]\circ G$, and the universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] yields the unique shift comparison $\sigma$ with $\sigma_{QK}\eta_{K[1]}=\eta_K[1]$. This is the shift commutation of [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], with the normalization fixed in the statement. On the K-injectives $L_I,P_I,H_I$, and on their shifts, both units are the identity-resolution identifications. Hence $\sigma$ is induced there by the termwise equality $G(K[1])=G(K)[1]$, using additivity, $G(-d)=-G(d)$. Consequently the displayed boundary equation is precisely the connecting square after applying $\mathcal G$, with its canonical shift comparison, and not just a commutative square on the first two arrows.

source.place: Tag 0A07 (lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim), first proof via the tower-topos square; Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective tower computation. Explicit cone-normalization refinement.

proof.text:
It remains to identify the first vertex after transporting the cone triangles to $R\lim$. In the chosen model, both derived composites in [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison] are computed without another resolution: $L_I$ is K-injective for $G$, and $J$ is K-injective for inverse limit. That node normalizes $a_M$ by the underived equality $G\lim=\lim G^{\rm Tow}$; hence $a_M$ is represented exactly by $\beta:G(L_I)\to L_J$. Step 6 yields
$Q(j_J)^{-1}\,Q(\theta)\,\mathcal G(Q(j_I))=Q(\beta)=a_M$.
Transport the three squares of Steps 4 and 7 along $Q(j_I)$ and $Q(j_J)$. Their components become $(a_M,\alpha_M,\alpha_M)$, and the last square reads
$a_M[1]\,\sigma_{R\lim_X M}\,\mathcal G(\delta_M)=\delta_{\mathcal G^{\rm Tow}M}\,\alpha_M$,
where $\sigma$ is the canonical shift comparison. All maps used are natural for strict tower maps. Their computed equations therefore hold for every derived tower, by the localization and K-injective computation [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. This gives the specified morphism of canonical Roos triangles.
